subject: Pioneer Health — on-prem inference throughput collapse and error spike
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@pioneerhealth.com
Date: 2028-08-24T18:12:00Z
Subject: Severe impact — on-prem cluster returning 502s and throughput drop

Marcus —

We started seeing a steep drop in throughput across our on-prem deployment at ~17:45 local. Requests that normally respond <200ms are timing out or returning 502s; p95 for inference jumped from ~220ms to 2.3s and error rate rose to ~6%. This is affecting production traffic to our triage assistant (approx 1k QPS at peak).

We restarted the inference nodes and the fronting Nginx at 18:00 which gave a small improvement, but errors resumed after ~30 minutes. Attached are the scheduler logs and a condensed trace (support_logs_20280824.tar.gz).

Can you jump on a call? We need next-steps and an ETA for stabilization — this is now on the CTO's radar.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Sr. SRE, Pioneer Health
Attachment: support_logs_20280824.tar.gz (1.2 MB)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T18:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe impact — on-prem cluster returning 502s and throughput drop

Elena —

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the logs. I'm escalating immediately. Quick ask before we join the call: can you confirm whether the model variant was changed in the last 24 hours or if any config push happened to the private control plane?

Immediate plan:
- I'm pinging Evelyn (runtime) and Naomi (deploy) to triage kernel-level saturation and recent rollouts.
- Please preserve the node console output and the /var/log/redwood/serving/*.log files; don't rotate them yet.
- If you can, capture a short perf top during a spike and drop it to the shared Drive link.

I'll set up a short war-room and invite your ops + our infra lead.

--
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@pioneerhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T18:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe impact — on-prem cluster returning 502s and throughput drop

On it. Initial observations from the logs Elena shared:
- Multiple TFLITE quantized model loads failed with repeated transient kernel OOM errors, followed by fallback to float kernel (higher memory + slower execution).
- KV cache hit rate dropped to ~12% during spike (normally ~78%) — suggests cache eviction storm.
- Several backend workers show high syscall latency (~10-30ms) consistent with heavy GC/IO stalls.

Immediate mitigations to propose (can be executed via your SRE team):
1) Temporarily reduce concurrency per worker to 2 and increase worker count to smooth memory pressure.
2) Revert recent model variant if the change correlates to the initial time window (18:10).
3) Reset KV cache (rolling) to restore hit-rate; use cache warmup script after reset.

I'll draft the exact commands for Pioneer ops. Marcus — recommend we get this in front of Mike O'Connor (CTO) in the call — he was cc'd earlier.

Evelyn
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: kv_cache_trace_0824.txt
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@pioneerhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-24T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe impact — on-prem cluster returning 502s and throughput drop

Team —

Thanks Evelyn. Naomi and I are preparing a concise runbook you can run with your ops team. Quick escalation note for context: Mike O'Connor (CTO) just joined the current war-room and is asking for an ETA to bring p95 back under 500ms. Naomi — can you prioritize the rollback check and a safe cache reset sequence? Laura — please prepare an exec-friendly one-pager (bullet list of root causes, mitigations taken, residual risk, recommended follow-ups).

Proposed short runbook (for Pioneer ops to execute in order):
A) Throttle frontend concurrency to 60% for 10 minutes (reduces queueing).
B) Apply worker concurrency change: set REDWOOD_WORKERS_PER_NODE=2 and trigger rolling restart of serving processes (one node at a time).
C) Run cache reset script with warmup: /opt/redwood/bin/reset_kv_cache --warmup /tmp/warmup_prompts.txt
D) If step B/C do not reduce p95 to <500ms in 20 minutes, revert to previous model variant: redwoodctl versions rollback --service inference --to <previous-version>

Naomi — I'll send the exact redwoodctl commands and a Link to the Drive folder with logs and commands.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook_commands.txt (sent to Drive)
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Connor <mike.oconnor@pioneerhealth.com>, ops@pioneerhealth.com
Date: 2028-08-25T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Severe impact — on-prem cluster returning 502s and throughput drop

Marcus / team —

We executed A/B/C per your runbook between 08:20–08:45 local. Immediate impact: p95 dropped from 2.3s → 420ms, error rate down to 0.6%. Cache warmup recovered hit-rate to ~70%. We left concurrency at reduced settings and are monitoring.

Mike is satisfied for now but asked us to coordinate a deeper post-mortem and capacity plan with Redwood (to include suggestions for safe default concurrency, automated cache warmup on deploy, and model variant rollout guardrails).

I'll drop the post-mortem notes into the Drive folder and grant Redwood SRE access. Thanks for the quick response.

—
Elena
Sr. SRE, Pioneer Health
